responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the National Semiconductor CR16 architecture, covering the target-specific part of code generation from backend configuration through RTL instruction selection to final assembly emission. Its main files divide the port into the target configuration header and options that define the CR16 ABI, data model, register file, storage layout, assembler conventions, and selectable architecture features; the C/C++ target-hook implementation that makes calling-convention, frame-layout, prologue/epilogue, interrupt-attribute, PIC and address-legitimization, constant-handling, and assembly-printing decisions; and the machine-description files that encode CR16 instruction patterns, predicates, and operand constraints for legal registers, immediates, addressing modes, and multiword operations. Together, this module translates GCC’s generic RTL and function state into CR16-specific stack usage, operand legality, instruction forms, and emitted assembly, distinguishing it from neighboring modules by owning the complete architecture port for CR16 rather than generic middle-end logic.
